title: Slope predicts a nearby change
purpose: Connect the derivative at a point to the sign and approximate size of a nearby function change.
assumptions: The learner can read a graph and evaluate a simple square.

blocks.purpose: Introduce the derivative as a local change predictor.
blocks.text: At x=2, f(x)=x^2 has slope f'(2)=4. For a small step dx, the change is approximately 4dx: the sign follows the step, and the size is scaled by the slope.

blocks.purpose: State the local approximation used for prediction.
Work one positive and one negative step without hiding the approximation.
blocks.text: For dx=0.1, the predicted change is +0.4; for dx=-0.1, it is -0.4. These are first-order predictions, not exact values.

blocks.purpose: Identify the calculus source behind the local-change framing.
blocks.label: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1

blocks.purpose: Check whether the learner can use the local slope.

exercises.prompt: For f(x)=x^2 at x=2, what derivative value predicts the change for a small step?
success_criteria: Can apply its sign to positive and negative small steps.
